chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said:

The divorce of a male slave is [valid] if he maraws a free woman, or if he marries the slave-girl of another people, [the divorce] is up to the slave; and if he marries his master's slave-girl, the one who separates them is he [the master], if he wishes, and if he wishes he can take her away without divorce.

key_terms.نَزَعَهَا: He took her away / removed her

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce a slave when his wife is his master's slave-girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the juridical nuance of a male slave's marital autonomy, distinguishing between wives of independent status versus those bound to his master. It highlights the master's unique prerogative to dissolve the union of his own slave-girl without a formal *talaq*, reflecting the hierarchical structure of slavery in early Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the interplay between personal agency and property rights within the household structure of the time.
